data.title: JPMorgan Chase Leads $3.5B Debt Refinancing for Zebra Technologies - News | ABL Advisor
data.summary: On Nov. 20, 2026, the Company closed on a $3.50 billion senior secured credit facility maturing Nov. 2031 with a pricing at Term SOFR + 1.00% when net debt leverage ratio is at or below 1.5x. The refinanced credit facility removed the credit spread adjustment which improves pricing by 10 basis points for, with respect to dollars, Term SOFR Rate loans. The refinanced credit facility also implemented 2.5 basis point favorable pricing with respect to commitment fees on revolving commitments when [...] Zebra Technologies Corporation, a global leader in digitizing and automating workflows to deliver intelligent operations, today announced actions to refinance its debt and expand liquidity. JPMorgan Chase Bank was the lead left arranger on the structuring and syndication of the refinanced credit facility, and Zebra Technologies engaged Sidley Austin LLP as counsel for the transaction.Debt Refinancing Highlights: [...] commitments when the Company’s net debt leverage ratio is below 2.5x. The refinanced credit facility has $250 million in increased capacity, consisting of a $1.75 billion revolving credit facility and $1.75 billion in term loans. The Company’s facility prior to refinancing was a $3.25 billion senior secured credit facility maturing May 2027 consisting of a $1.50 billion revolving credit facility and $1.75 billion of term loans.

data.title: Visa, Mastercard, JPMorgan Chase data leaked in ransomware attack | Fox News
data.summary: What JPMorgan Chase says about the cyberattack JPMorgan Chase confirmed that third-party service providers were targeted in a cyberattack. In a statement to CyberGuy, a JPMorgan Chase spokesperson said, "Based on our investigation so far, we believe the attackers accessed certain marketing data held by those vendors, which may include some customer names and email addresses." [...] JPMorgan Chase says it will contact affected customers where appropriate and offer support, including complimentary credit monitoring. If you receive a breach notification, confirm that it came from your financial institution before clicking an enrollment link or sharing personal information. Credit monitoring can help you identify suspicious changes to your credit reports. However, it cannot stop someone from sending phishing emails or impersonating your bank. You should also be suspicious of [...] So far, the companies' statements point primarily to customer information held by outside service providers. Mastercard says its payment network remains secure, while Visa says payment card numbers were unaffected. JPMorgan Chase has identified potentially exposed marketing data. There has been no verified indication that customer banking passwords were stolen or that hackers accessed funds through this incident.

data.title: What the JPMorgan Chase, Visa, and Mastercard Vendor Breach Teaches Us About Third-Party Risk - SecurityScorecard
data.summary: Three of the largest names in global finance disclosed data exposures on the same day, and attackers breached none of them directly. On November 19, 2026, JPMorgan Chase, Mastercard, and Visa each reported a cyberattack on a third-party service provider. This third-party data breach shows how one vendor’s compromised credentials can quietly reach the customers of many companies at once. [...] - JPMorgan Chase: Attackers targeted third parties that provide services to the bank and accessed certain marketing data those vendors held. That data may include some customer names and email addresses. Chase found no disruption to its services and will offer complimentary credit monitoring to affected customers where appropriate. [...] The payment networks stayed online, and no card numbers were leaked. Still, the incident carries a lesson for every security and risk leader: your exposure extends as far as your vendors’ access does. What Happened in the Chase, Visa, and Mastercard Vendor Breach All three disclosures point to marketing and contact data exposed through outside providers.
